content_html:
Consciousness Windows Across Scales

Consciousness (as we currently understand it) seems to require rich complexity, fast, recurrent causation (feedback loops), and relative stability to form memory and self-models. This suggests a scale-dependent window: too small → too fast and fragile (decoherence, noise); too large → too slow and diffuse (lightspeed limits, sparse connectivity).

The “sweet spot” appears where complexity, speed, and system boundaries align to enable integrated, recurrent causation.

Quantum / Subatomic

~10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹⁰ m; timescales ~10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹² s

  • Pros (speculative): High parallelism; exotic correlations.
  • Cons (evidence-based): Ultra-rapid decoherence erodes coherent states on femto–picosecond scales, far shorter than neural integration windows (ms).
  • Assessment: Unlikely to support stable, memory-bearing consciousness by known mechanisms. Orch-OR remains controversial.

Microbial / Cellular

~10⁻⁶–10⁻³ m; ms–s dynamics

  • Cells have signaling networks, but limited global integration.
  • Single neurons are not typically conscious in isolation; integration across networks matters.
  • Assessment: Proto-computation and responsiveness, but unclear/low for full-blown consciousness.

Human / Organisms

~10⁻³–10¹ m; ms–seconds dynamics

  • High integrated information (Φ) with fast recurrent loops; temporal integration windows tens–hundreds of ms.
  • Empirically associated with reportable experience.
  • Assessment: Plausible / observed.

Socio‑technical / Ecosystem / Planetary

~10³–10⁷ m; seconds–years dynamics

  • Rich distributed cognition and ecological memory across agents/artifacts/environments.
  • But integration is loose, bandwidth limited, and lacks the unified causal borders IIT posits for consciousness.
  • Assessment: Collective intelligence yes; unitary consciousness doubtful by current theories.

Galactic / Cosmic

~10¹⁹ m and above; years–eons dynamics

  • Light‑speed and sparsity of interactions prevent rapid closed causal loops.
  • Philosophical positions like cosmopsychism propose a universe‑level subject; not empirically confirmed.
  • Assessment: Speculative; incompatible with known communication limits for brain‑like awareness.

Constraints

  1. Integration speed: brains bind information over tens–hundreds of milliseconds (multisensory & perceptual “binding windows”).
  2. Decoherence vs. stability: at quantum scales, coherence collapses too fast to support memory‑bearing states; at cosmic scales, signal delays are too long for unified loops.
  3. Boundaries: theories like IIT require a system with clear borders and high irreducibility; brains fit, loosely coupled mega‑systems don’t.

Alternatives

  • Panpsychism / Cosmopsychism: experience is fundamental and scale‑independent; a universal field of consciousness (UFC) underlies matter.
  • Middle‑world intuition: our evolved cognition is tuned to a mid‑scale; extremes look alien (quantum weirdness, relativistic spacetime).
